jobs.title: AI Solutions Engineer, Customer Agents
jobs.description: **About Attuned Intelligence** ------------------------------ Attuned Intelligence is automating patient access for community health centers and health systems. We build AI\-powered voice agents that automate how patients enter, navigate, and stay connected to care — from the first phone call to a scheduled visit. Every missed call at a health center is a missed appointment. Every language barrier is a gap in care. We exist to close those gaps. Our platform handles hundreds of thousands of calls per month across multiple languages, routing patients to the right care team on the first try — and integrating directly with Epic to automate scheduling, appointment management, and clinical workflows. We're a fast\-moving team backed by a deep understanding of agentic systems and healthcare operations with a mission\-driven approach to building technology that makes care more accessible and equitable. **The role** ------------ We're looking for a hands\-on AI solutions engineer to build and improve agents for our healthcare customers. You'll translate requirements gathered by the Customer Delivery team into reliable agent capabilities, developing prompts, conversation flows, and tool integrations that improve patient access and reduce administrative work. Partnering with platform engineers, you'll prototype new capabilities, test the complete experience, and turn recurring customer needs into reusable solutions across the Attuned platform. Success means customers have reliable agents, know how to use them effectively, and can see measurable improvements in their operations. **What you'll do** ------------------ * **Build and validate customer solutions.** Design prompts, conversation flows, knowledge content, and tool integrations. Test complete experiences against realistic scenarios and customer expectations. * **Develop new agent capabilities.** Translate customer problems into new agent behaviors, tools, and workflows. Prototype and validate solutions, building directly where appropriate and partnering with platform engineers on capabilities that require product or infrastructure changes. * **Test and troubleshoot systematically.** Develop scalable testing systems that can run representative customer scenarios. Reproduce failures, distinguish prompt and configuration issues from model or platform problems, and verify that changes improve the intended behavior. * **Drive ongoing customer outcomes.** Use call results and feedback gathered by Customer Delivery to recommend and implement agent improvements and identify opportunities to expand the agent's usefulness. Measure progress through successful task completion, patient experience, and reduced staff effort while preserving privacy and appropriate human handoffs. * **Turn customer learning into product improvements.** Identify needs shared across customers and contribute reusable capabilities, implementation approaches, and recommendations for the product roadmap. **What you'll bring** --------------------- * 3\-5 years experience with hands\-on experience building LLM\-based agents, conversational experiences, or workflow automations, with concrete examples of what you built and how you tested it. * Experience with voice AI, conversation design, speech recognition, or text\-to\-speech systems. * Strong writing and structured reasoning: you can turn an ambiguous request into clear instructions, decision logic, and observable success criteria. * Practical programming or scripting ability, plus comfort working with APIs, JSON, version control, and logs to build and debug workflows. * A methodical approach to troubleshooting. You investigate what happened, reproduce the problem, and validate the fix against the actual user experience. * Clear communication with technical and nontechnical teammates, including explaining dependencies and surfacing missing requirements early. **Helpful experience** ---------------------- * Agent tool calling, evaluation frameworks, or automated scenario testing. * Customer implementations, technical support, or another role that translates real\-world operating requirements into working software.

jobs.title: Backend Software Engineer - Simulations
jobs.description: **About Rune** Rune Technologies builds mission\-critical software for military logistics and sustainment. Our flagship product is TyrOS, an AI\-enabled logistics command and control platform that gives commanders a single, real\-time operating picture of their sustainment fight, from inventory and distribution to medical and operational planning, even in degraded and contested environments. We're not a traditional defense contractor. We're a small, fast\-moving team that combines deep operational experience in and with the DoD with the software discipline of the best product companies, and we apply that combination to a customer set that desperately needs it. We stay close to our users by embedding directly with military units during exercises and rotations, and we ship constantly based on what we learn. The U.S. military and its allies face a real logistics modernization problem. We're building the software to solve it. **About the Role** At Rune Technologies, we are building the logistics technology backbone that the U.S. and allied militaries need to dominate in large\-scale combat operations. As a Backend Software Engineer at Rune, you will be part of a high\-impact team working at the intersection of advanced logistics algorithms, modern AI\-enabled software, and complex system integrations — all in support of the warfighter at the tactical edge. You'll join us in our mission to bring 21st\-century software to the sustainment domain: modernizing inventory management, transportation optimization, and predictive planning with state\-of\-the\-art user experiences. You'll work closely with a team of experienced engineers, product designers, and operational experts who care deeply about delivering real\-world impact. As our Backend Software Engineer for Simulations, you will own the simulations workstream within TyrOS, working closely with our forecaster lead and the broader platform team. The primary focus is Rune's forecasting system, building the production software that models, predicts, and reasons about logistics outcomes in complex operational environments. This role calls for a strong software engineer who is also mathematically and scientifically fluent: someone who can work in formulas, reason about physical systems, and build production\-quality software around that reasoning. **What You'll Do** * Build and own production\-grade simulation and forecasting software, with a primary focus on Rune's logistics forecaster. * Work with mathematical models, numerical methods, and scientific formulas to implement software where correctness is defined by the underlying physics or math, not just user acceptance. * Collaborate closely with the forecaster lead and platform team to integrate simulation capabilities into TyrOS workflows. * Participate in technical design discussions and code reviews, contributing to a culture of engineering rigor and mission focus. * Triage and debug issues in production, ensuring reliability and rapid iteration in support of operational needs. * Work closely with engineers, product managers, and military stakeholders to ensure simulation and forecasting systems meet real\-world sustainment requirements. **Qualifications** * 4\+ years of experience in software engineering, with demonstrated experience building software in a scientific or mathematically complex domain: sensor algorithms, motion planning, simulation, forecasting, or similar. * Ability to work with mathematical models and numerical methods in code; comfort reasoning about correctness in terms of physics or math, not just software behavior. * Proficiency in Python, C\+\+, or Go. * Strong software engineering foundation \- this role requires production\-quality engineering, not analysis or research. * Math or science background, through degree, graduate work, or professional domain experience. * Strong sense of ownership and a bias for action. **Desired Qualifications** * Experience at a defense\-adjacent autonomous systems company in a hands\-on engineering capacity * Degree or graduate degree in a scientific field such as physics, applied mathematics, aerospace, or mechanical engineering. * Familiarity with numerical simulation frameworks or scientific computing libraries. * Experience deploying software to production environments, including cloud (AWS, Kubernetes) and edge infrastructure. **Benefits** Rune offers top\-tier benefits for full\-time employees to include a full suite of insurance options at no cost for employees and low\-cost to spouses and dependents. Highly competitive equity grants are also included in the majority of full time offers and are considered part of Rune's total compensation package. Benefits include: * Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans; premiums 100% covered by Rune for all employees; exceptionally low premiums for spouses and dependents * Basic life insurance and disability 100% covered for all employees by Rune; option to purchase additional life insurance available * ‘Take the time off that you need, when you need it’ paid time off, not accrual based * Generous company holiday calendar including a holiday shutdown in December * Supportive leave of absence program including time off for military service, medical events, and parental leave * Full 401(k) retirement plan for all full\-time eligible employees * Company\-funded commuter benefits * Free access to on\-site gym at office Compensation Range: $190K \- $210K

jobs.title: CNC Systems Service Engineer (FANUC)
jobs.description: **Build, restore, and elevate machine performance** --------------------------------------------------- Join a team that keeps precision manufacturing moving. You’ll travel to customer sites to install new CNC equipment, bring legacy machines back into spec, and partner with engineering to crack the toughest anomalies. Every day, you’ll combine sharp diagnostics with clear communication to deliver results that customers can measure in microns and minutes. **What you will do** -------------------- * Plan and execute CNC machine tool installations in line with manufacturer standards; commission systems and demonstrate full operation. * Leverage schematics, blueprints, manuals, and wiring diagrams to determine procedures and resolve issues. * Tune drives, align assemblies, and troubleshoot electrical/mechanical/hydraulic/pneumatic subsystems to maintain tolerance. * Use diagnostic instruments and hand tools to repair equipment; collaborate with engineering on edge‑case faults. * Inspect completed assemblies and verify that all moving parts operate correctly within expected limits. * Engage daily with project managers (internal and external), supervisors, and customers to report status and plan next actions. * Define the tools, equipment, and parts required to execute the scope of work efficiently. * Deliver routine service and co‑create preventive maintenance schedules with customers. * Assemble, align, and install equipment; verify precision using calipers, micrometers, height gauges, and similar tools. * Immediately report any incidents or errors; take on additional duties as assigned. **Qualifications** ------------------ * High school diploma or equivalent plus hands‑on CNC machine technician experience. * Applied math proficiency with fractions, percentages, ratios, and proportions. * Proficient with PCs for email, records, databases, documents, spreadsheets, and basic graphics; above‑average Microsoft Office skills. * Valid driver’s license and ability to travel 15–20% with overnight stays, including trips of 1–2 weeks as needed. * Required: FANUC control expertise. **How you work** ---------------- * Attendance you can count on. * Dependability—trusted to follow procedures and deliver. * Safety first: clean workspace, proper storage, guards in place, and strict adherence to SOPs, safety rules, and GMPs. **Physical and environmental realities** ---------------------------------------- * About 20% stationary while operating equipment; frequent walking to access tools, parts, and machines; constant operation of powered equipment. * Regularly work above and below machines; extensive fine and gross manipulation. * Clear verbal exchange with team members; near‑range detection of defects and mechanical issues to inform actions. * Routinely lift/push/pull/move up to 50 lbs; carry and load parts and tools. * Occasional exposure to humidity, moving parts, fumes/airborne particles, and caustic/toxic chemicals; typical noise is moderate, with exposure to loud machinery. * PPE is mandatory around machinery and electrical currents; expect warmer conditions while wearing PPE in hot months. **Technical domains you’ll use** -------------------------------- * Preventive maintenance planning * Mechanical troubleshooting * 120/208/240/480‑volt power systems * Electrical installation, troubleshooting, and repair * Relay testing * Pneumatics troubleshooting * Precise tape‑measure use * Service orientation in customer settings * Maintenance and repair fundamentals * Industrial electrical experience * Rigging and load handling * Field service readiness * Industrial electrical systems * Workplace safety and EHS management * Hydraulic systems and components * Equipment diagnostics and troubleshooting * Mechanical systems and component repair * Lockout/Tagout (LOTO) * Electrical panel installation * Spindle maintenance and repair * Reading electrical schematics * Low‑voltage cabling installation * Equipment installation and wiring * Access control systems * Equipment repair and maintenance * Equipment installation * Aerospace manufacturing exposure **Accessibility** ----------------- Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions.

jobs.title: Enterprise Technology Solutions Engineer (AI & Automation)
jobs.description: About Linea Energy Linea Energy is a leading independent power company dedicated to developing, building, and operating renewable energy projects across the Americas. Our mission is to provide sustainable energy solutions that empower communities and drive the transition to a clean energy future. Headquartered in San Francisco, California, Linea Energy is committed to innovation, excellence, and the highest standards of environmental stewardship. About the Position We are seeking an Enterprise Technology Solutions Engineer to join Linea Energy on a full\-time basis, preferably based in any of our existing office locations: Austin, TX, Chicago, IL, or San Francisco, CA. The successful candidate will own the design, build, and deployment of AI\-driven automations and custom internal applications that eliminate manual work across development, legal, finance, GIS, and execution teams. This role sits at the intersection of enterprise architecture, software development, and business operations, with a strong emphasis on agentic workflows, LLM\-powered automation, and rapid AI\-assisted development. The ideal candidate will be resourceful, technically versatile, and comfortable working across disciplines in a fast\-paced renewable energy environment, and will also share responsibility for technology operations, administration, and security for the company’s information technology environment. Responsibilities and Essential Functions * Key individual within company responsible for enterprise software architecture and solutions * AI Automation and Agentic Workflows: Design, build, and operate AI\-powered automations and agent\-based workflows (using LLM APIs, Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, and workflow platforms) that connect to the systems where work already happens, such as Sitetracker/Salesforce, SharePoint and Microsoft 365, Notion, financial and data\-room platforms, and document repositories. Prioritize automations by business impact and measure hours saved, accuracy, and adoption. * Application Development: Design, build, and maintain custom internal tools and applications using Python and JavaScript that put AI automations in the hands of development, legal, GIS, finance, and execution teams. * AI\-Assisted Development: Leverage modern AI\-assisted coding tools (e.g., Claude Code, Copilot, Cursor) to rapidly prototype, iterate, and deliver production\-quality software, applying appropriate testing, code review, and deployment discipline to AI\-generated code. * Cross\-Functional Collaboration: Partner with stakeholders across the organization to identify high\-value automation opportunities, map current workflows, gather requirements, and translate business needs into technical solutions. Train and support employees in adopting AI tools and automated workflows. * Enterprise Integration: Build and maintain integrations between internal systems of record, cloud services, and third\-party platforms using APIs, webhooks, and MCP connectors to streamline data flows and reduce manual processes, with attention to reliability, monitoring, and error handling. * GIS and Spatial Applications: Develop or enhance GIS\-enabled applications, spatial data pipelines, and automated spatial analyses to support energy project siting, analysis, and reporting. * Code Quality and Version Control: Maintain clean, well\-documented codebases using Git, participate in code reviews, and follow best practices for collaborative development, including testing and evaluation of AI\-driven workflows. * AI Governance and Data Protection: Help define and enforce policies for responsible AI use, including approved tools and models, data classification, handling of confidential project, financial, and counterparty information, prompt\-injection and data\-leakage safeguards, human\-in\-the\-loop review for high\-risk automations, and logging and auditability of automated actions. * Cloud Infrastructure: Deploy and manage applications, automations, and services within Azure cloud environments, including VMs, app services, functions, and data storage, along with access control, cost monitoring (including AI/LLM usage costs), backups, and patching. * Technology Operations and Administration: Serve as a technical resource for select IT operations, help manage the IT consultant, and and support procedures, and coordinate with third\-party IT providers, AI and software vendors on evaluation, licensing, renewals, and issue resolution. jobs.title: Forward Deployed Engineer
jobs.description: **Who We Are** -------------- A few weeks ago a 95\-year\-old patient called one of our practices. She apologized for being long\-winded before she’d said much of anything. “I promise my mind is still very sharp,” she said; you could hear in her voice that she’d been made to feel otherwise. Our agent didn’t cut her off. It listened. She thanked it at the end of the call for being so patient. She probably didn’t know she was talking to AI. But she felt that someone had listened. Most voice agent companies in healthcare are racing to solve one thing: getting patients off hold fast enough to schedule an appointment. We think that’s the wrong finish line. The moment a patient calls is just the beginning: there’s the referral fax, the insurance check, the prescription refill, the follow\-up, the billing. Most of it is invisible to the patient and exhausting for the practice. We’re building the platform that handles all of it, with the patient at the center of every touchpoint. We’re 2 years in and working with 400\+ medical practices across 27 specialities, including primary care, dermatology, optometry, and mental health. One Medical's founder is an investor. We've raised over $13M in VC funding and grew ARR 10x last year, which means it's a great time to join. **The Role** ------------ You’d be one of the first few dedicated Agent Engineer at Parakeet. There’s no playbook for this yet… you’d be writing it. In practice: you’re in customer calls four or five times a week, translating what you hear into decisions and working prototypes (sometimes before the call even ends). You’re the person who holds context on both sides: what the customer needs, what our platform can do, and what the gap is. You make the call on what gets built now, what gets pushed, and what becomes a roadmap item. Nobody’s going to make that call for you. Healthcare scheduling is not OpenTable. A doctor might only want to see new patients in the morning and existing patients in the afternoon because that doctor runs out of steam by afternoon (and yes, that’s a real rule we’ve had to build for). Multiply that by every practice, every specialty, and every quirk that’s now yours to translate into something an AI agent can execute. If that sounds like a fascinating puzzle rather than a grind, you’re probably the right person for this role. Then there's the part that makes this more than an implementation job: the best version of this role is someone who hears something from a customer on Monday and has a working prototype to show them by Tuesday. Prototypes are the new PRDs. The gap between “I heard something interesting today” and “let me show you what I built” should be measured in hours, not sprints. Here’s a good example of how we operate: a customer told us they were drowning in 50,000 unprocessed faxes a month. The next day we had them forwarding faxes into our system. Within two weeks we had an MVP running on actual production faxes: a tool that reads incoming referrals and prior authorizations and calls the patient to schedule them. That product is live today, and what used to take 5 to 7 days now takes just one minute. The FDE is the tip of the spear on what we discover and build next. Most large healthcare practices are used to waiting 6\-9 months for something like that. We did it in 2 weeks. **A Day in Your Life** ---------------------- No two days look the same, but here’s a realistic sketch: ***Morning****:* You jump on a call with a new eyecare customer’s office manager to walk through how they handle appointment recalls. You learn they have a specific routing rule: patients who haven’t been seen in 18\+ months need to be scheduled with their original provider, but if that provider has left, they need a fallback with a different call script, and insurance needs to be checked again. You’re taking notes and already sketching how to express this in the platform before she’s even finished explaining it. ***Late morning****:* You’re configuring a deployment for a multi\-specialty medical group in NYC. Their eClinicalWorks integration needs a tweak to pull the right appointment types for their specialty scheduling flow. You push a fix, test it against their sandbox, and watch the agent nail the booking. (Small win. Onto the next one.) ***After lunch****:* Weekly sync with one of our largest enterprise accounts: a dermatology group with hundreds of locations across the country. Their VP of Operations is a fast talker with a top\-notch Hawaiian shirt game. He’s both deeply knowledgeable about their practice and genuinely excited about what’s possible with technology. Today he flags that they get 30,000 voicemails a month that nobody’s getting to. You’ve been thinking about this since hearing something similar from another customer last week. You sketch a quick prototype with Claude Code—what insights to derive, what automated actions the agent could take—and share your screen to get his reaction. The VP says: “I love it. Tell me the S3 bu n the sidelines. He’s senior enough to mentor everyone, but humble enough that nobody feels mentored. Also inexplicably West Coast for an East Coast guy. * **Mimu** joined a month ago and has already built a Claude onboarding agent that turns customer docs and meeting transcripts into a configured agent, shrinking implementation time from 5 days to 2 hours. In his spare time he’s building a 3D printed clock. (The clock was not on anyone’s roadmap.) * **Tyrone** commutes from Berkeley by bike every day, which is either impressive or unhinged depending on how you feel about the Bay Bridge. He loves climbing and will invite every new hire to go with him. * **Tom** runs Customer Success and will be your closest partner here. We took him to a client in Orlando once and they said it was the smoothest IT implementation they’d ever experienced (because: Tom). He’s technical enough to dig into a problem before passing it to engineering, funny enough to defuse a tense customer call, and somehow finds time to win Tuesday night softball championships. He also has a dachshund named Wanda who is, by any measurable metric, our most effective marketing asset. * **Jung** (co\-founder, CEO) was patient number one at One Medical: he helped the founder build the first financial model before the practice had a single location. He also built the compliance program there from scratch, which is why we're already SOC 2 and HIPAA compliant. He has a PhD in operations research, which means the person running ops here thinks like an engineer. On the weekends you can find him at the farmers market selling kimchi in honor of his mother. * **Eric** (co\-founder, CPO) was my college classmate, and we played on the same rec league basketball team before we decided to build together. He was working in ML/NLP before ChatGPT existed, which means he knew this business was possible before most people were even asking the question. Eric’s the reason we’re building in healthcare specifically… but I’ll let him tell you that story. * **Me** (Aaron, co\-founder, CTO): Eric and I have been friends since before any of this existed. I think the best thing I can say about what it’s like to work with me is that he’s still here. **Requirements** ---------------- 2\-5 years of engineering experience. Comfort working across the full stack: you don’t need to be a specialist, but you need to be able to move fast across frontend, backend, and integrations. Experience with Python is a plus. More important than any specific technology: you’ve shipped real things, you’ve talked to the people using them, and you’ve made judgment calls without waiting for someone to define the problem for you. **Interview Process** --------------------- We move quickly: you’ll hear back within 48 hours after each round. This can be as fast as two weeks end\-to\-end. * 30\-minute founder intro call * 1\-hour technical phone screen: you’ll problem\-solve through an evolving technical challenge * Full\-day onsite in San Francisco. We’ll work through real customer problems together. If your schedule allows, we’d love to make this a paid 3\-day work trial. We think it’s the best way for both sides to know if there’s a real fit. * Reference checks Offer ### **Benefits** * Excellent health, dental, and vision insurance * Free dinner * Espresso machine (pull your own shots) * Gourmet snacks and lots of Diet Cokes * Fitness stipend * Commuter benefits * Unlimited PTO * 401(k) * Relocation stipend ### **Our Office (The Nest)** In\-person, Downtown SF by Montgomery BART. After years of remote work, we wanted to be in the same room again to brainstorm, whiteboard, and actually enjoy each other’s company. There’s high ownership, no BS meetings, and a ton of gourmet snacks. Once a week we also get out of the office for a team lunch… because some of the best conversations happen away from the whiteboards. *Include a in your application for extra credit.* * Aaron, Co\-founder \& CTO Compensation Range: $150K \- $200K

jobs.title: Founding Sales Engineer
jobs.description: **About us** ------------ MintMCP helps companies put agents to work safely. We exist to help companies do more of their work with agents, and we build the infrastructure that makes a company's own work runnable by them. That has to start from trust. Our first product is an MCP gateway that gives those agents governed access to company data and tools. Before agents can touch Slack, GitHub, Jira, Snowflake, internal databases, or production systems, you need to know what they can reach, what they did, and why they were allowed to do it. Most people carry far more permissions than any single task needs. If an agent uses your token directly, it inherits all of them. MintMCP scopes that access down to exactly what an agent needs to do its job and captures the data flows and audit logs security teams need. From there we are building the rest of the agent stack: connectors, monitoring, sandboxing, long\-running agents, and memory, with the goal of becoming the system a company's work runs on. We work in person in the San Francisco Bay Area. The structure is flat and the market moves fast, so you have a lot of latitude over what you work on and how. We are AI\-native. Everyone uses Claude and Codex every day, and we have more agents than employees. They run in Slack alongside the team and handle sales, marketing, deal ops, and engineering on the same gateway we sell to customers, and we are building an entire company operating system around them. Since launching in February 2026, we have grown to 50\+ paying customers, with strong inbound demand. Customers include Coursera, Arlo, and Braze. We are backed by Cowboy Ventures and Coatue, with angels including Frederic Kerrest (Okta), Michael Grinich (WorkOS), Andrej Karpathy, Jeff Dean, and Scott Belsky. Our founders are machine learning experts from Stanford, Berkeley, and CMU, with applied research at Google Brain and Waymo, and one co\-founded Coursera. **The job** ----------- You are our first sales engineer, and you own the technical sale. You work alongside our AEs as a partner on every deal, from the first demo through the POC to close. You lead technical discovery, run the demo, design the POC, and answer every question about how MintMCP would actually deploy in a customer's environment. The AE owns the commercial side of the deal and you own whether the buyer believes it will work, so you have as much say in how a deal gets won as anyone on it. Depending on the deal's complexity, you may stay involved after the signature: helping get customers live, doing hands\-on advanced setup (e.g., custom MCP servers, middleware), and stepping into support. You are also one of the strongest voices customers have inside MintMCP. You'll see a lot of customer environments up close, so you bring what customers need straight to product and engineering, push for it, and speak confidently to the roadmap in front of a technical buyer. We'd rather you tell us what customers actually need than tell customers what they want to hear. As our first sales engineer, you'll help shape how the function grows: the playbooks we run, how we onboard new people onto the team, and the pillars that guide it. We have strong inbound and a team of five AEs who need you on every deal. The role is in person, with travel to meet customers. **About you** ------------- * You have 4\+ years of experience, ideally as a sales engineer, solutions engineer, presales engineer, solutions architect, or forward\-deployed engineer, and you understand how a technical sale moves from first call to signature. * You have sold complex technical products (e.g., infrastructure, security, dev tools), not apps. * You come from software engineering or a logic\-based field (e.g., CS, math, physics, engineering). That said, your track record matters more than the degree. * You are hands\-on technical. You can build a custom integration, debug a deployment, and get a POC working yourself. * You communicate clearly with engineers and executives in the same meeting, and you can explain why the product matters to the business as well as how it works. * You make the reps around you more effective, and AEs want you on their deals. * You are AI\-native, or will get there fast, and are genuinely curious about AI, agents, and how companies adopt them. * You move fast without a lot of process, and you would rather build the motion than inherit one. **Bonus** --------- * DevOps background, and you enjoy being customer\-facing. * Experience with MCP or AI agent tooling. **What we offer** ----------------- * Competitive base, variable, and significant equity. * Ownership of the technical sale, and a real say in how the sales engineering function grows. * A front\-row seat to agentic AI, with room for special projects like building internal agents. * Direct access to the CEO, customers, and product decisions. * Health benefits, on a team that puts family and health first. *Prefer to have your agent apply? Point it at* *https://www.mintmcp.com/hiring/mcp*

jobs.title: Head of Product
jobs.description: About Luca IQ Luca IQ is building a modern tax engine for accounting firms. Nearly every tax return prepared by a CPA in America runs through one of a small number of tax engines built decades ago. Rebuilding that infrastructure means translating tens of millions of words of tax law, regulations, and IRS guidance into software that can calculate returns correctly and consistently. We're building an API\-first tax engine designed from the ground up to calculate, validate, and file U.S. tax returns. Luca IQ is one of eight IRS\-approved tax engines for CPA firms. We’re building the infrastructure that will power the next generation of tax preparation software. About the role Professional tax preparation begins with a messy set of documents and ends with a return that must be accurate. Luca IQ is building the modern tax engine and application that makes that process faster, more reliable, and easier for tax professionals. We are looking for an AI engineer to own the intelligence layer across that workflow. You will design and maintain systems that turn documents into usable tax data, help tax professionals identify missing or inconsistent information, and review completed returns before filing. This is not a role focused on a generic chat experiences. You will build production AI systems that operate on real financial documents and work alongside a deterministic tax engine, where accuracy, traceability, and thoughtful human control matter. The Team Luca IQ was founded by Angelo Policicchio, a CPA, and Akash Sadashivapeth, who met at Harvard Business School. Our engineering team brings decades of combined experience building deterministic engines for the financial services industry, where accuracy is non\-negotiable. We’re building Luca IQ because nearly every tax return prepared by a CPA in America runs through one of a handful of tax engines built in the 1990s, and we’re building the first modern, API\-first, IRS\-approved engine to replace them. What You’ll Work On **Document collection and classification:** Build systems that collect client documents and identify what they are, including tax forms, financial statements, receipts, and supporting materials. **Extraction and normalization:** Turn structured and unstructured documents into reliable, usable data. You will design workflows to extract fields, preserve source context, resolve ambiguity, and route low\-confidence results for human\-in\-the\-loop review. **Agentic return review:** Build agents that examine a completed return alongside its source documents and relevant tax context. The system should identify missing information, inconsistencies, and potential errors, then explain findings clearly and propose corrections for a tax professional to review. **The AI experience:** Shape how tax professionals understand, trust, and act on AI output. This includes confidence, citations to source documents, review workflows, correction flows, and clear boundaries between suggestions and final decisions. **Evaluation and reliability:** Build the evaluation, observability, and feedback systems needed to measure extraction quality, agent performance, and user outcomes over time. What We’re Looking For * Experience building robust document OCR and extraction systems, including working with PDFs, forms, scanned documents, and financial data, and applying modern LLM\-based methods for document understanding, parsing, and structured data extraction. * Experience designing scalable evaluation frameworks that reliably benchmark quality, including defining evaluation datasets, ground\-truth labels, scoring methodologies, and statistical analyses for structured and unstructured documents. * Strong judgment about evaluating design, observability, reproducibility, and human\-in\-the\-loop workflows. * A bias toward shipping and learning from real\-world document and model behavior, paired with a high bar for accuracy, auditability, reliability, and actionable measurement. What Success Looks Like **In your first 30 days,** you’ll understand and optimize the document and return\-preparation workflow, ship meaningful improvements, expand extraction coverage, and pinpoint the most time\-consuming manual steps where AI can improve accuracy, speed, or consistency. **By 60 days,** you’ll own a production workflow for document classification and extraction with clear quality metrics and a feedback loop from users. **By 90 days,** you’ll have established the foundation for expanding AI across the application into an AI\-powered review experience that helps tax professionals catch issues earlier and prepare returns with greater confidence. How We Work We are a small team with high ownership and little separation between product and engineering. You’ll work directly with tax professionals, collaborate with engineers building the tax engine and application, and make consequential decisions about how AI becomes part of a new tax platform. Pay: $125,000\.00 \- $200,000\.00 per year Benefits: * 401(k) * Dental insurance * Health insurance * Life insurance * Relocation assistance * Vision insurance Work Location: Hybrid remote in Chicago, IL 60654

jobs.title: People Operations Specialist

Our founding team previously built and operated SpaceX’s Autonomous Spaceport Droneships, which are among the most advanced autonomous maritime systems ever deployed. Today, we work with leading U.S. operators to bring that same rigor and systems thinking to the next generation of maritime infrastructure. **About the Role** ------------------ Oceanus is hiring its first in\-house People Operations Specialist to take ownership of the People foundations we’ve built and carry them into the company’s next stage of growth. We believe a company should be as innovative as its products. People Operations should create leverage for the business and its employees through clear systems, thoughtful use of technology, low friction, and an environment where people can do their best work. This person will inherit strong foundations. scale. **Key Responsibilities** ------------------------ **People Strategy \& Programs** * Build Oceanus’s one\-to\-three\-year People strategy and roadmap, aligning priorities with company plans, handoff through offboarding, including onboarding, employee changes, records, leaves, accommodations, system access, and internship operations. * Serve as a trusted point of contact for employees, handling questions and sensitive matters with responsiveness, discretion, and sound judgment. * Continuously improve the employee experience by gathering feedback, identifying friction, and making processes clearer and easier to navigate. **Payroll, Benefits \& Compliance** * Run payroll and timekeeping for exempt and hourly employees, including timecard review, off\-cycle payroll, leave adjustments, and final pay. * Manage health benefits and the company’s 401(k) in partnership with brokers and providers, including open enrollment, employee support, and reconciliation. * Build practical compliance systems and coordinate with outside counsel and company partners on state and federal requirements, sensitive employee matters, equity, agreements, and insurance. **Systems, Workplace \& Company Operations** * Own Rippling and connected People systems, using thoughtful workflows and automation to improve accuracy, reduce manual work, and create leverage. * Build scalable People Operations resources, including SOPs, employee guides, compliance calendars, manager tools, and self\-service resources. * Support Carta administration, board consents, annual filings, permits, insurance certificates, and related company documentation. * Support workplace operations across Oceanus’s El Segundo locations, including vendors, facilities, supplies, equipment, and access. **Your Background** ------------------- * 3\+ years of experience across People Operations, HR Operations, or HR generalist work, ideally within a startup, small company, or lean People team. * Experience building new People processes or programs, not only administering established ones. * Direct experience supporting both exempt and hourly employees. * Hands\-on experience with payroll, benefits, employee lifecycle operations, and HR compliance. * Strong working knowledge of California employment requirements. * Experience administering an HRIS, including building workflows, managing permissions, connecting systems, and maintaining reliable data. Rippling experience is strongly preferred. * A track record of taking manual, unclear, or inefficient processes and turning them into systems that work. * Resourceful and comfortable moving between long\-term planning, program design, daily operations, and unexpected problems. * Strong judgment and discretion when handling sensitive employee and company information. * Curious about how technology, automation, and AI can make People Operations more effective. * Able to work on\-site across Oceanus’s El Segundo locations. **Additional Experience We Value** ---------------------------------- * Experience as the first or only People Operations hire at an early\-stage company. * Experience supporting field engineers, forward\-deployed teams, manufacturing teams, or another operational workforce. * A background in hardware, aerospace, defense, robotics, maritime, or another technical environment. * Experience building performance, leadership development, learning, or total rewards programs from the ground up. * Experience with Carta, equity administration, Human Interest, leave management, or outside employment counsel. **Work Environment** -------------------- * On\-site with the team at our office in El Segundo, CA **Compensation and Benefits** ----------------------------- We are open to a wide range of experience levels. The expected salary range for this role is $105,000 \- $175,000\. Final compensation will be determined based on experience, skills, and scope of the role. We offer a comprehensive benefits package that includes: * Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision coverage * Generous Equity participation * Fully stocked kitchen and catered lunch every day * Onsite EV charging * Flex Paid time off and company holidays * 401(k) traditional and roth options * Additional benefits that support your health, growth, and well\-being **Why Oceanus, Why Now** ------------------------ Maritime operations are at the edge of a revolution. Regulatory, economic, and geopolitical pressure is accelerating technology adoption, and U.S.\-aligned infrastructure is more valuable than ever. Oceanus is building on hard\-won operational experience, including work on autonomous maritime systems supporting missions like SpaceX droneships, and have deep operator engagement with strong product\-market alignment. jobs.description: Agents don’t wait for approval. They call models, tools, and APIs thousands of times before anyone reads the first answer. Someone has to decide which of those calls go through, what they’re allowed to cost, and who’s accountable for them. That’s Zuplo: the unified gateway for APIs and AI — one programmable policy engine for the models your apps call and the agents that call you. Teams route their AI and MCP traffic through our AI Gateway and MCP Gateway, so every agent call is accounted for. We’re hiring a Senior Software Engineer to help build and run it. You’ll own major pieces of the gateway runtime, the control plane, and the systems that keep them reliable. Our stack spans Kubernetes, several clouds, and the edge, and we care more about how fast you learn than which tools you already know. **What you’ll do** * Design how agents making thousands of model and MCP tool calls are authenticated, metered, rate\-limited, and observed. * Ship new guardrails and routing policies for the AI Gateway, such as model fallback, spend caps, and prompt\-injection checks, behind canaries, alerts, and a clear rollback. * Build and operate the services behind all of this across Kubernetes, multiple clouds, and the edge, mostly in TypeScript and Go, with some Rust. * Own what you ship in production. When a customer reports something vague, you take it to a root cause, a fix, and a dashboard so it can’t hide again. * Work across the rest of Zuplo too. API management (portal, keys, rate limits, GitOps) and our monetization service run on the same policy engine. * Keep what’s already shipped healthy, including the customer issues that make it to engineering. * Improve how we ship, from CI/CD to infrastructure as code (Terraform, Pulumi, or similar). * Work with product, developer experience, and customers to turn a fuzzy idea into a scoped plan, then ship it end to end. **What you bring** Required: * Experience (typically 5\+ years) building and running distributed systems in production. * Hands\-on Kubernetes experience, or proof that you can get there fast. Tell us about a time you picked up an unfamiliar system quickly. * Fluency in TypeScript/Node.js or Go, and a willingness to work in the other. * Experience with AWS or GCP. * Working knowledge of networking: DNS, TLS, and load balancing. * Experience with CI/CD, observability, and incident response (for example, Prometheus, Grafana, or OpenTelemetry). Preferred: * Hands\-on experience with LLM APIs, MCP, or agent frameworks, and with the security, cost, and reliability problems that come with them. * Experience building or running proxies, gateways, or edge and serverless runtimes. * Experience with multi\-cloud or hybrid deployments. **How you work** * You use AI every day, and you can explain what it built: why it works and what it could break. * You care about alignment. You want to know that systems and agents are doing what we intended, and you build ways to find out fast when they aren’t. * You care more about impact than about the code itself, and you reach for the 80/20 solution first. * You’re relentlessly resourceful, with a bias toward doing things *today*. * You fix what’s broken, whether or not it’s yours. **About Zuplo** Zuplo was founded by the folks behind Auth0’s developer experience and Azure API Management. What drives us is building products developers love to use. We are not a 9\-to\-5 company. Hours are flexible, and we expect high output and quality. We work hard, learn fast, and push boundaries. We respect work\-life balance, and we also expect real commitment when deadlines approach or challenges arise. In return, you’ll grow fast and make a real impact on a fast\-growing company going after a multi\-billion dollar market. If you want your contributions recognized and your skills challenged, alongside a team that cares as much as you do, Zuplo is the place for you. **What we offer** * Competitive salary, plus equity options so you share in what we build. * Unlimited PTO. We encourage everyone to take at least 20 days off a year. * Flexible working hours. * Funded team off\-sites in beautiful and fun locations. * A high\-end MacBook Pro and the best tools available. * Continuous learning and professional development, including exploring new AI tools. **Location and work authorization** In the San Francisco Bay Area, you’ll work from our office three days a week. Elsewhere in North America, the role is remote. You must already be authorized to work in the country where you’re based. We’re unable to sponsor visas for this role. **Interview process** * Initial screening with our CTO * Take\-home exercise (a few hours) * Technical interview with the rest of the team over Zoom * Final conversations with our founder and co\-founder

jobs.title: Senior Software Engineer, Payments
jobs.description: Alt is unlocking the value of alternative assets, starting with the $5 B trading\-card market. We let collectors buy, sell, vault, and finance their cards in one place and we are backed by leaders at Stripe, Coinbase, Seven Seven Six, and pro athletes like Tom Brady and Giannis Antetokounmpo. Our next frontier is real\-time pricing at scale—the Alt Value that powers every trade, loan, and product on the platform. **The Role** ------------ An auction closes and every seller in it gets paid in the same moment, each against a different fee schedule — some by ACH, some by wire, some instant. A buyer funds a five\-figure purchase and the bank returns it three days later. A webhook arrives twice, out of order, from a provider that was down for an hour. Every one of those movements has to reach the right account, on the right rail, at the right time, and land in the ledger exactly once. That is the whole job. You own how money physically moves at Alt: the providers, the rails, the orchestration layer that routes between them, and the risk posture that keeps a marketplace of high\-value transactions safe. The ledger team owns the record; you own everything that happens between a customer's bank and that record. You are not building a checkout flow. You are building the liquidity that makes this marketplace work. The KPI: 99\.99% reliability on gateway and banking integrations, and a time\-to\-funds for sellers and borrowers that we measure, publish, and beat every quarter. In payments, "mostly working" is a failure. The people who are great at this have integrated a provider that lied to them, and they design for the third retry, the late return, and the duplicate callback because they've been on the wrong side of all three. **What You'll Own** ------------------- **Rails and money movement.** ACH origination and returns, RTP and other instant rails, wires, cards, and stablecoin settlement. A $300K wire and a $300 ACH debit are different products with different controls, and you'll design for both. Credit\-push rails change what you can auto\-charge and when funds are final — you'll own those product consequences, not just the integration. **Provider architecture and orchestration.** Multi\-PSP integrations built so the next one isn't a rewrite, and a single orchestration layer that routes each movement to the right provider by cost, speed, and health. Webhooks, idempotency, retry semantics, state machines, failure modes on the third retry, and provider failover that nobody notices. **Payouts and collections.** Getting sellers and borrowers their money faster than anyone else in this market: instant payout options, batch payouts at auction close, and the rail and timing choices that make them safe. On the other side, cash advance disbursement and the scheduled auto\-pay batches that collect repayments run on your rails. The ledger team decides what a pending balance means; you decide how and when the money actually moves. **Risk on high\-value flows.** The fraud, dispute, and chargeback posture for a marketplace where one bad transaction is a five\- or six\-figure problem. Holds, limits, and settlement windows set with data — and you'll know what each one costs in conversion. Step\-up verification triggered by risk signals rather than blanket friction. **Payment operations.** When a transfer is stuck, a return code is unfamiliar, or a provider goes quiet mid\-batch, you find out why. You'll own the tooling that lets operations and support answer "where is my money" without paging an engineer, and you'll feed clean, complete processor data to the ledger team's reconciliation so their breaks are real breaks and not missing webhooks. **The posting contract, from the producer side.** Every movement you originate lands in the ledger through a typed contract the ledger team owns. You'll build against it, push on it when a new rail doesn't fit, and guarantee exactly\-once delivery into it. **The trade\-off calls.** Shipping speed against uncompromising reliability; build custom versus buy an orchestration platform. You'll be asked to defend both directions. **The team.** Be a multiplier through rigorous code reviews, technical documentation, and mentorship. **How You'll Use AI Here** -------------------------- We don't want to hear that you use Claude every day. Everyone does. We want to know what you've built with it. Concretely, in this role: * Turn a payment provider or bank partner integration spec into a typed client and a test suite in an afternoon instead of a sprint — including the ACH return codes and reversal paths nobody wants to hand\-write * Stand up a rail simulator that produces the failures a sandbox won't: a late return, a duplicate callback, a partial reversal, a webhook that arrives twice out of order, a settlement that lands after the window closed. Then run the orchestration layer against it * Build an agent that watches provider health, webhook lag, and return rates, and proposes a routing change or  e the failure mode is a five\- or six\-figure problem and someone notices immediately. * You're API\-native. Webhooks, idempotency, eventual consistency, and exactly\-once delivery are your default vocabulary. * Strong SQL and relational design. You know how to write a transaction that won't fail under load — including at auction close and during scheduled auto\-pay batches. * Marketplace or two\-sided flow experience. Buyers and sellers, settlement between them, and the timing tension that creates. * An obsession with reliability. You think deeply about idempotency, race conditions, and what happens on the third retry. * Product\-owner thinking. You don't just build a pay button. You understand the flow of funds and how to communicate financial status clearly to a user who is worried about their money. * Pragmatism. You know when to build a custom internal solution and when to leverage a third party to get the job done. **Strongly preferred:** direct experience with Stripe, Plaid, Airwallex, PayPal, Modern Treasury, or Increase, and with evaluating or building a payment orchestration layer across more than one of them. **Strong plus:** fraud, dispute, or chargeback work on a marketplace; hands\-on with risk tooling like Sardine, Sift, or Stripe Radar; enough React and TypeScript to ship the payment\-method and payout surfaces you own. **Bonus:** distributed systems; stablecoin or on\-chain settlement; KYC/KYB, bank partnership, or bank\-sponsor program exposure; the alternative asset space. You collect, or you have a view on where this market is going. **How We'll Interview You** --------------------------- We'll be specific so you can prepare. Before any of it: download the app, put a card up, make a bid, and try selling — go through the workflows. Every round assumes you've used the product, and we expect your point of view to sharpen as you go. For this role, look specifically at the deposit, payment method, and payout surfaces. * **Recruiter screen** — 25 minutes, Google Meet. Come ready to talk about the metric you own today and how you're performing against it, why Alt specifically, and how you're actually using AI. We'll answer your questions. * **Hiring manager** — 45 minutes, Google Meet. Be ready to go deep on the provider integration or money\-movement system closest to your own hands: what you built versus inherited, the trade\-offs you made, and what you'd change now. * **Technical screen** — 60 minutes. A hands\-on working session on a rail behaving badly — duplicate and out\-of\-order webhooks, a late return, a provider that acks and then times out — and a payout batch that has to complete exactly once. Think out loud. * **Architecture and system design** — 60 minutes. Design a payment orchestration layer under real constraints: two providers, failover mid\-batch, instant and batch payouts, a risk hold on a five\-figure transfer, and a ledger contract you don't control. We'll push back on at least one of your choices on purpose — how you take that matters as much as the design. * **Culture interview** — 30 minutes. How you work with the people who depend on your systems — operations, finance, support, and the customer on the other end of a held transfer. * **Leore, our founder and CEO** — 30 minutes. Everyone who joins Alt meets Leore. Come with a point of view on where you'd take Alt's money movement first. * **Reference check(s)** — 15 minutes with a former manager(s). **What we offer:** ================== ***For full\-time Employees*** * We cover 85% of your medical, dental, and vision, and up to 50% for dependents. HSA/FSA available * Generous PTO that people actually take * Parental leave at full salary * $200/month wellness \+ $100/month home office stipend * Free DoorDash Pass membership, because dinner shouldn't be a decision * Remote\-first (for most positions), with WeWork access when you want a room with other humans * 401(k) * Alt Equity to all full\-time employees Compensation Range: $200K \- $220K

jobs.title: Software Engineer
jobs.description: **Help build software that makes finding, applying for, and managing job opportunities easier.** Applyline brings job discovery, application preparation, automated workflows, email, and application tracking into one workspace. We’re looking for a Software Engineer to help improve the product and build reliable services behind it. The work spans the user\-facing application, backend automation, and our employer hiring tools. What you’ll work on * Build clear, responsive interfaces for onboarding, profiles, job discovery, applications, and hiring. * Develop backend services that prepare application materials, process jobs, and track workflow progress. * Integrate job boards, employer application systems, email providers, and payment services. * Improve browser automation so workflows handle changing forms, missing information, verification steps, and failures clearly. * Build our hiring platform, including Careers pages, applicant intake, candidate pipelines, and job distribution. * Improve application performance, database queries, background workers, monitoring, and recovery. * Write meaningful tests, investigate production issues, and carry changes through deployment. What we’re looking for * Experience building web applications with TypeScript or JavaScript, React, and backend services. * Familiarity with relational databases, API integrations, authentication, and background processing. * The ability to debug problems across the interface, server, database, and third\-party services. * A practical approach to testing, security, and handling sensitive user information. * Clear communication about implementation choices, progress, and problems. * An interest in taking ownership of a feature from development through production. Experience that would be useful * Next.js, Node.js, and PostgreSQL. * Playwright or other browser automation tools. * AI integrations using structured outputs, validation, and evaluation. * Email, Stripe, recruiting systems, or job\-board integrations. * Deploying and operating containerized applications. How to apply Submit your résumé on our Careers site: https://careers.applyline.ai/careers/3137a055\-cd80\-4d62\-9aa5\-c6a71e887ad7\. Include a short example of something you built, a difficult technical problem you solved, or a production system you helped improve. A portfolio or GitHub link is welcome if you have one. This is a full\-time, fully remote Software Engineer role with an annual salary of $100,000 USD. A closer look at the work This role connects the product people see with the services that make it work. A feature may start with an applicant uploading a résumé, continue through a background worker preparing application materials, and finish with a status update or an email. You will help make those transitions reliable and understandable. The employer side has a similar journey: a hiring team creates a role, publishes it, receives candidate applications, and follows up through the hiring pipeline. Product and interface development Build interfaces that make the next action clear. Improve form validation, loading states, error messages, accessibility, and responsive layouts. Help users understand what has been saved, what is in progress, and what needs their input. Work on application review screens, profile editing, résumé previews, and employer workflows. Keep important actions usable when services are slow or a third\-party integration is unavailable. Backend systems and integrations Develop APIs and background workflows that can recover from failures. Keep task state durable, avoid duplicate actions, and record evidence when an external system confirms an outcome. Integrate email events, payments, job data, and employer forms using the appropriate API or browser workflow. Treat timeouts, retries, changing form fields, and partial responses as normal engineering problems that need clear behavior and useful diagnostics. Automation and AI features Help improve the preparation of résumé edits, cover letters, and application answers. Use structured outputs and validation so generated material remains grounded in information the user provided. Build tests around the difficult cases, including missing information and mismatched inputs. For browser workflows, distinguish a completed submission from an attempted click, and make uncertain outcomes visible rather than reporting success prematurely. Hiring tools Improve the Careers site, application intake, résumé storage, screening questions, written interviews, and candidate communications. Make it easy for a hiring team to see an applicant’s contact information and application history. Help connect approved employer accounts and build job distribution workflows that can verify the published listing. Candidate assessment should support the hiring team; people remain responsible for hiring decisions. How we approach engineering Start by understanding the user’s problem and the existing workflow. Break the work into changes that can be reviewed and tested. Explain important tradeoffs, document integrations where needed, and investigate the cause of a failure rather than only its symptom. Pay attention to sensitive data, authentication boundaries, and what information is passed to outside services. Prefer useful tests that exercise meaningful behavior over checks that simply repeat the implementation. Examples of impact * Reduce the time it takes to load an applicant’s workspace without loading unrelated data first. * Make an application workflow recover cleanly after an email verification or an employer form change. * Improve a résumé review experience so users can see, accept, and confirm each change. * Build an applicant intake flow that reliably saves a résumé and sends the next\-step email. * Add monitoring that makes stalled tasks, provider errors, and unexpected duplicate actions easy to investigate. These examples describe the work you may contribute to; they are not a requirement to have built every one of these systems already. What to include in your application Tell us what you personally contributed to a project, not only what the team shipped. A useful example explains the problem, the technical choices you made, the result, and what you would improve next. If you share a code sample, choose work you are allowed to share and remove confidential information. You do not need to disclose credentials, customer data, or proprietary source code. The application process Step 1: Submit your résumé and answer the three screening questions on our Careers site. We save your application and email a receipt to the address you provide. Step 2: If you opt in on the form, we email a private link for a written interview with more detailed, role\-specific questions. The link expires after 14 days. Your answers may be reviewed with AI assistance against job\-related criteria; a person makes hiring decisions. You can contact info@applyline.ai to request an alternative. The hiring team reviews applications and contacts candidates about any further steps. Submitting an application or completing the written interview does not guarantee an interview or an offer. Employment details This is a full\-time, fully remote Software Engineer role with an annual salary of $100,000 USD. Pay: $100,000\.00 per year Work Location: Remote

The Arango Contextual Data Platform connects fragmented enterprise data with LLMs, copilots, and AI agents through a simplified architecture delivered out of the box. Learn more at arango.ai, LinkedIn, and G2\. **About the role** Arango is hiring a Customer Solution Architect to be the primary professional services interface between Arango and the customers deploying our AI product suite. You own the technical relationship end to end, from first discovery through production and expansion. Your job is to turn a customer's problem into a working architecture on Arango's multi\-model platform and its GraphRAG and knowledge\-graph capabilities, prove value early, and guide the customer's team through deployment and adoption. The role sits where solution architecture, graph data modeling, and applied AI meet. It suits someone who can hold a design conversation with a customer's chief architect in the morning and review a GraphRAG retrieval design with their engineers in the afternoon. Deep graph expertise is not optional here. It is the core of how Arango's AI suite delivers value, and the CSA is expected to be the customer's most trusted source of graph and GraphRAG design judgment. **Key responsibilities*** Own the technical customer relationship as the primary professional services contact across the full lifecycle: discovery, design, pilot, production, and expansion. * Run discovery with customer sponsors, domain experts, and operators to identify high\-value use cases for Arango's AI product suite, and qualify them against real business outcomes. * Design target architectures on Arango's multi\-model platform, including graph data models, AQL query and traversal patterns, and GraphRAG retrieval design tailored to the customer's domain. * Define success criteria, SLAs/SLOs, data access and governance requirements, and a phased delivery plan from proof of value to production. * Build reference implementations and prototypes that prove value early: graph schema, data connectors, GraphRAG pipelines, tool and agent orchestration, APIs. * Guide production deployment into secure, observable services alongside the customer's engineers, with CI/CD, infrastructure\-as\-code, and proper testing. * Architect retrieval across graph traversal, vector search, and hybrid approaches (chunking, embeddings, ranking, caching), and orchestrate tool and agent calls. * Establish evaluation practices and iterate on prompts, models, retrieval strategy, and graph structure using offline and online metrics and A/B tests. * Design data pipelines (ETL/ELT), vector indices, graph ingestion, and metadata governance. * Define monitoring for quality, drift, hallucination and guardrail events, latency, and cost, and stand up alerting and dashboards with the customer. * Architect role\-based access, secrets management, audit logging, PII redaction, and content safety controls. * Meet customer compliance requirements (SOC 2/ISO 27001, GDPR/CCPA, HIPAA as applicable). * Produce architecture documentation, runbooks, and reusable patterns, and train customer engineers and end users. * Act as the voice of the customer to Arango's product and engineering teams, shaping the roadmap with what we learn in the field. This is an AI\-first leadership role requiring deep AI/ML expertise, strong engineering judgment, and the ability to build and scale multidisciplinary technical teams. We are looking for a technical leader who can connect AI, machine learning, data, and engineering into scalable systems and lead the organization responsible for building them. What you will bring Significant experience building and deploying AI and machine learning systems in production at scale. Strong technical background in modern AI/ML, including generative AI, large language models, agentic systems, model evaluation, and traditional machine learning. Demonstrated experience leading multidisciplinary organizations across AI/ML, data science, and data engineering. Strong production engineering and systems architecture experience, with the ability to take AI capabilities from prototype through production. jobs.title: RF Field Engineer
jobs.description: Airtower Networks delivers total managed services and mobile connectivity for the commercial real estate and enterprise sector. Inc. Magazine has named us one of America’s Fastest\-Growing Companies. We design, deploy, own and operate in\-building cellular and public safety networks that tenants, first responders, and building owners rely on every day. If you want a fast\-growing company that invests in your development, pays competitively, and promotes from within, read on. **The role** The RF Field Engineer owns the hands\-on technical delivery of large in\-building DAS and managed networks, from first site survey to commissioning, close\-out, and ongoing performance. You will be the technical bridge between design engineering, deployment crews, carriers, and the authorities having jurisdiction (AHJs). This role is centered on field execution rather than design ownership. You will validate that what was designed is what gets built, prove it with test data, and keep it performing to carrier KPIs and client SLAs. * Location: Remote, based in the DC Metro Area, Atlanta, North Carolina or near a major airport hub * Travel: Regular travel to customer sites across the nation * Reports to: Director of Network Engineering * Employment type: Full\-time, exempt What you’ll do * Surveys and pre\-construction * Perform pre\- and post\-contract RF site surveys and benchmark data collection (walk testing, scanner and UE data) * Join site walks and pre\-construction meetings as the primary technical resource * Review construction drawings, iBwave designs, and RF schematics against site conditions; flag gaps to design engineering early Installation validation and testing * Act as liaison between design engineering and deployment teams so networks are built as designed * Validate installation of DAS head\-ends, remotes, RF sources (BDA, eNB/gNB, small cell), DC power plants, and low\-voltage circuits * Perform CW testing, spectrum analysis, segment and system sweep testing, PIM, and OTDR testing * Use small hand tools for minor installation tasks, rack\-and\-stack, and cable terminations Commissioning and acceptance * Lead commissioning, integration, and optimization of cellular and public safety DAS, including uplink/downlink link balancing and power sharing * Prepare systems for carrier integration and acceptance against carrier KPIs * Lead public safety ERCES commissioning and oversee AHJ inspections and third\-party testing for code compliance (NFPA 1225 / IFC 510\) Maintenance and support * Monitor systems remotely and respond to trouble tickets, onsite or remote, to meet client SLAs * Perform fault analysis, interference mitigation, preventive maintenance, and annual public safety retesting * Execute system modifications, expansions, and upgrades with project managers and design Documentation and communication * Produce commissioning reports, test results, as\-builts, and close\-out packages * Communicate status and findings clearly to clients, carriers, contractors, and internal teams * Follow industry safety standards, local codes, and Airtower safety protocols on every site **What you bring** * 3\+ years of hands\-on field experience with cellular or public safety DAS (installation, commissioning, troubleshooting) * Solid grasp of RF propagation and antenna theory, with working RF math: link budgets, power sharing, noise figure, and uplink/downlink balancing * Proven commissioning and optimization experience on at least two of: JMA, SOLiD ADRF, Andrew, Comba, Fiplex, Nextivity, SOLiD, Airspan. * Proficiency with spectrum analyzers, cable/antenna analyzers, PIM testers, OTDR, CW signal generators, and RF scanners * Ability to read construction drawings, iBwave designs, and RF schematics * Basic networking and LAN configuration for DAS management and remote monitoring * Experience wiring DC power plants and low\-voltage circuits * Clear written and verbal communication; comfortable presenting results to clients, carriers, and inspectors. * Ability to work independently, travel regularly, and hold a valid driver’s license **Nice to have** * Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering or a related field (equivalent field experience considered) * Experience on both cellular and public safety networks * OEM certifications (e.g., CommScope, JMA, SOLiD, ADRF) or industry credentials such as NICET, iBwave, or FCC GROL * Familiarity with NFPA 1221/1225, IFC 510, and local AHJ requirements for ERCES * Experience with carrier integration and LTE/5G NR KPIs on large venues or neutral\-host systems * Exposure to small cells, private LTE/5G (CBRS), or Wi\-Fi * Experience mentoring or leading field technicians **Tools and platforms you’ll use** Category \- Examples * DAS / BDA OEMs + JMA, ADRF, CommScope, Comba, Fiplex, Nextivity, SOLiD, Corning * Test equipment + Spectrum analyzer, cable and antenna analyzer, PIM tester, OTDR, CW signal generator, power meter * Survey and data collection + RF scanners, UE\-based data collection, post\-processing software * Design and documentation + iBwave, Bluebeam, Microsoft Office **Work environment** * Active construction sites, ceilings, risers, telecom rooms, and rooftops * Climbing ladders, lifting and carrying test equipment up to 50 lbs, and working in tight spaces * Occasional after\-hours or weekend work for cutovers, inspections, and urgent trouble tickets **Salary Range:** * Base salary: $100K\-$125K + *We have listed this salary range with a good\-faith minimum and maximum compensation. The final salary will vary depending on factors like experience, geographic location, and skills.* **Benefits:** At Airtower Networks we recognize our ultimate success depends on our talented and dedicated workforce. We understand the contribution each employee makes to our accomplishments and so our goal is to provide a comprehensive program of competitive benefits to attract and retain the best employees available. * Insurance: Medical, dental, and vision * Retirement: 401(k) \[with company match] * Paid time off and holidays * Company vehicle or mileage reimbursement, phone, and test equipment * Paid OEM training and certifications, with a clear path to Senior RF Field Engineer and beyond * Additional Incentives: This position may qualify for bonus opportunities based on factors like individual and company performance metrics. **Equal opportunity** Airtower Networks believes that diversity and inclusion among our teammates is critical to our success as a company. We seek to recruit, develop, and retain the most talented people from a diverse candidate pool. Airtower Networks is committed to providing an environment of mutual respect where equal employment opportunities are available to all applicants and teammates without regard to race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, national origin, age, physical and mental disability, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, genetic information, military and veteran status, and any other characteristics protected by applicable law.

You will engage with AWS product owners to influence product direction and help our customers tap into new markets by utilizing GenAI along with AWS Services. Amazon.com’s recommendations engine is driven by machine learning (ML), as are the paths that optimize robotic picking routes in our fulfillment centers. Our supply chain, forecasting, and capacity planning are also informed by ML algorithms. Alexa is fueled by Natural Language Understanding and Automated Speech Recognition deep learning; as is Prime Air, and the computer vision technology in our new retail experience, Amazon Go. We have thousands of engineers at Amazon committed to machine learning and deep learning, and it’s a big part of our heritage. AWS is looking for a Generative AI Solutions Architect who will be the Subject Matter Expert (SME) for helping customers in designing solutions that leverage our Generative AI services. You will interact with customers directly to understand the business problem, help and aid them in implementation of generative AI solutions, deliver briefing and deep dive sessions to customers and guide customer on adoption patterns and paths for generative AI. As part of the Generative AI Worldwide Specialist organization, you will work closely with other Solution Architects from various geographies to enable large\-scale customer use cases and drive the adoption of Amazon Web Services for GenAI services. You will interact with other Data Scientists and Solution Architects in the field, providing guidance on their customer engagements. You will develop white papers, blogs, reference implementations, and presentations to enable customers and partners to fully leverage Generative AI services on Amazon Web Services. You will also create field enablement materials for the broader technical field population, to help them understand how to integrate AWS Generative AI solutions into customer architectures. You drive effective feedback gathering from customers, and you distill and translate that feedback into clear business and technical requirements for product and engineering teams to review. You must have deep technical experience working with technologies related to large language models including LLM architectures, model evaluation, and fine\-tuning techniques. You should be proficient with design, deployment, and evaluation of LLM\-powered agents and tools and orchestration approaches. You must have experience with embedding model fine tuning and retrieval method evaluation approaches. You should understand the security and compliance requirements for ML/GenAI implementations. You must have experience with LangChain, LLAMAIndex, Data Augmentation, Responsible AI, and Performance Evaluation frameworks. You should have experience architecting end to end ML/Gen AI applications for customers using AWS services and Well Architected Framework. Candidates must have great communication skills and be very technical, with the ability to impress Amazon Web Services customers at any level, from executive to developer.
